svg.title: RIEMANN R6 — Heights and the covolume bound: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 6 in one poster: its 32 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-covolume-bound, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: Each member of the families of chap-families carries lattices M_j of rank D. This chapter proves that their covolumes are bounded in terms of the size parameters of the family (thm-covolume-bound). The proof that families exist (thm-family-data-exists) needs this bound. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)
Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines (four on a short card). The footer gives its file and
line in the mirror and the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges. A proof use outside the chapter is counted, not drawn. Rows: a card's row is one above the highest card whose proof uses it, or higher
where that makes room; a card sits under the cards that use it where it can. A short card shows four lines of the signature and one paragraph of the proof.

text.tspan: Functorial resolution of singularities in characteristic

svg.text: There is a rule that assigns to every variety over a field of characteristic zero a resolution of its
singularities, and to every embedded variety a strong embedded resolution (a sequence of
blow-ups in smooth centres after which the strict transform is smooth and meets the
exceptional divisor with simple normal crossings). The rule commutes with smooth morphisms
and with extensions of the ground field.
Run the canonical principalisation algorithm, which is correct by
thm-principalisation-reduces-dimension, on the ideal of the embedded variety.
Functoriality comes from the fact that every invariant the algorithm uses is local and
commutes with smooth morphisms and field extensions.

The lattices of the families of def-family-data have bounded covolume. That is, for every
class of families satisfying the family hypotheses there is C_0 ≥ 0 such that for every large x,
every member at scale x and every admissible choice of its data, the lattices M_j of rank D on
the indefinite side satisfy (2)/(D [K:ℚ])log covol(M_j) ≤ ell_j(C) for all j and all
C ≥ C_0, where K is the field of definition and ell_j(C) is the bound that the size parameters
of the family prescribe. We have not unfolded the bound ell_j(C).

text.tspan: 3 · The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….

text.tspan: 1. Mean arithmetic volumes on flag towers

svg.text: This section proves the lower bound for mean arithmetic volumes of automorphic line bundles
on unitary Shimura varieties (thm-mean-arithmetic-volume-lower-bound), which the
height argument of sec-ht-deep-covers uses. Over an integral model we build a tower of
flag bundles of the Hodge bundles, whose root line bundles make up the automorphic line
bundles, and prove the volume theorem on it (thm-good-towers-from-arakelov-inputs).
The proof needs two facts: the arithmetic self-intersections, less their main term, change sign
under simple reflections of the Weyl group (lem-weyl-antisymmetry-intersection), and
at the finite places the de Rham and Hodge–Tate flags have the same Chern classes (
lem-de-rham-hodge-tate-flag-comparison), by Dieudonné theory over mathcal O_C (

Heights are computed on integral models. This section builds integral models of unitary
Shimura varieties inside Siegel moduli schemes (thm-unitary-integral-models), starting
from full-level models whose universal abelian scheme carries an ample line bundle with theta
coordinates (thm-full-level-ample-models). It also gives Mumford's construction of
degenerating abelian varieties over complete normal local rings (
thm-mumford-degeneration), which the boundary charts of sec-ht-toroidal use.
Arithmetic intersection numbers need proper models, so the chapter works on toroidal
compactifications. This section proves that unitary Shimura varieties have smooth toroidal
compactifications with boundary a divisor with simple normal crossings and a logarithmic
minimal compactification and the blow-up that a cone decomposition determines, we build
rigid charts of Mumford type at the boundary points (thm-unitary-rigid-boundary-charts
) and compute the Kodaira–Spencer map in them (
